detail.body:
## Purpose

Add the Prometheus histogram `vllm:kv_offload_tiering_promotion_latency_seconds` for secondary-to-primary
promotion attempts, labeled by tier.
The histogram measures elapsed time from `TransferJob` creation until the tier reports completion. It includes time waiting in the tier queue and failed promotion attempts. It does not use `JobResult.transfer_time`, which measures
active data transfer only. P2P promotions are measured even when their `JobResult` has no `transfer_time`.

Buckets range from 5 ms to 60 s.

## Test Plan
```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_metrics.py  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/test_manager.py -v
```
## Test Result
Add the actual command results after running the tests on the final branch.

inline_comments.body:
[P1] Record promotion latency for the P2P tier

This observation is nested under completed_job.transfer_time, but the real P2P load-completion path appends JobResult(job_id=lr.job_id, success=lr.success) in tiering/p2p/manager.py and never populates that field, whose default is None. Every completed P2P promotion therefore skips this block, leaving the new histogram with no observations for the P2P tier even though its documentation promises per-job latency from secondary tiers. The added test only supplies transfer_time manually and does not exercise a backend. Please time the P2P load lifecycle and populate JobResult.transfer_time with a completion regression, or explicitly exclude/document tiers that cannot emit this metric.

inline_comments.body:
Thanks for picking this up, and sorry for the slow reply on my side.

I re-checked the current head `a5c9c974bad3af159a1b2734a02978bbc18f2e62` and the P2P gap I raised is closed. `P2PSession` now stamps `submitted_at` when a load is issued and builds `LoadResult(..., transfer_time=time.monotonic() - load.submitted_at)` on `transfer_done`, and the manager forwards `transfer_time=lr.transfer_time` into `JobResult`. The observation in `_observe_finished_job_stats()` is therefore reachable for real P2P promotions instead of being skipped on the `None` default.

The two regressions cover both directions I was worried about: `test_load_transfer_time_propagates_to_job_result` pins the propagation through the manager, and `test_tiering_metrics_tracker_records_promotion_latency_histogram` asserts a promotion records the observation while a cascade job records none. That resolves my finding.

One note so my confirmation is not over-read: this is a source and regression review only — the functional suite has not run on this head, so I am not claiming CI evidence.

Claude:
monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: clock) patches the stdlib module attribute, so every caller in the process sees a constant clock. Any while time.monotonic() < deadline loop on another thread in the same pytest process (or a timeout plugin) hangs rather than fails. Scope it to the module under test instead.

The tier `transfer_time` strictly` measures the time the tier spent actively transferring the data. Like in the FS tier here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/6ca2b23e22aab8534e00a85e8ec5222508a6ecf3/vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/fs/thread_pool.py#L175 

Promotion Latency, IIUC, is the e2e job time. For example, in the context of the FS tier, the Promotion Latency time is, 
 "time the job waits in the thread_pool queues + transfer_time". 
 
I think we should rather compute this at the manager level ? wdyt ?
